messages:
Emily Tran: hey @security — got an SMS a few minutes ago asking me to 'reverify Redwood access'. link was short.ly/rdw-verify (screenshot attached). did NOT click. posting here in case others saw it :eyes:

Lina Chen: thanks emily. can you drop the screenshot + the raw SMS text into #security-phish-submissions or paste here? also, did the SMS show our org name or look like generic login?

Emily Tran: pasted screenshot in thread. text was: 'Redwood account requires re-verification. Click short.ly/rdw-verify to continue.' it looked like our SSO page (logo), but domain was weird. no username/password entered.

sec-bot: Incident created INC-2026-142. Triage queue notified. Adding @sandbox-bot to analyze the URL.

sandbox-bot: fetching short.ly/rdw-verify -> follows redirect chain (3 hops) -> final host: evil-login[.]cloud/path
sandbox snapshot: returned HTML form styled like Redwood SSO, form action -> https://collect-creds[.]ru/submit
verdict: malicious credential harvesting. indicators: evil-login[.]cloud, collect-creds[.]ru, short.ly redirect chain. ETA for cleanup tasks: immediate block recommended.

Jon Patel: confirmed sandbox output. quick curl trace I ran:
```
$ curl -I https://short.ly/rdw-verify
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://redir1.evil-login-cloud[.]com/track?x=abc
...
```
page contains obfuscated JS that posts to collect-creds[.]ru. no payloads, just form POST.

Maria Gomez: containment steps (executed):
- Added evil-login[.]cloud and collect-creds[.]ru to org DNS blocklist (Cloud DNS & network firewall).
- Short URL sinkhole request submitted to security DNS team (ticket DNS-419).
- Rotated any service tokens referenced in logs (none found so far).
- Reached out to security ops to watch auth logs for spike in failed logins from external IPs.

Lina Chen: thx. Emily — since you didn't click, no immediate user action needed beyond being vigilant. For the record, please confirm you didn't forward or share the link.

Emily Tran: confirmed I didn't click or forward. only forwarded screenshot here. :thumbsup:

Lina Chen: follow-ups:
- Security will send a short all-staff note (no panic) with indicators and guidance to IGNORE the link and report. (Dave can you draft?)
- Add these domains to email gateway blocklist and URL rewriting rules.
- Add this attack sample to our phishing training corpus for next drop.

Dave Howard: I can draft the note. suggested copy: "We detected a malicious SMS impersonating Redwood SSO. If you received a message asking you to reverify via short.ly/rdw-verify or similar, do NOT click. If you clicked, immediately change your Redwood password and enable MFA and DM security." will post draft to #all-hands for review.

Jon Patel: also recommend we add a temporary rate/geo block for suspicious login attempts from the IPs associated with that domain. pushing for a 24h watch rule in WAF.

Maria Gomez: monitoring set for 72h. SIEM alert rule created: auth.event contains evil-login-cloud OR collect-creds. will escalate if any events.

Lina Chen: post-incident actions (owners):
- update phishing playbook with SMS handling nuances (Lina)
- add sample to phishing training (Training Team, Maria)
- email + comms (Dave)
- verify short URL provider (Jon) to request takedown (if possible)
- Timed follow-up postmortem in 1 week (Lina + Maria)

Emily Tran: thank you all for the quick response. learned something new — appreciate the fast triage team.

sec-bot: INC-2026-142 -> status: contained. follow-up: playbook update and awareness email scheduled.
